title: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

reading.body:
An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride struck and killed a duck in Austin, Texas while operating in autonomous mode with a human safety operator present. The vehicle did not slow down or avoid the animal despite it being in a predictable location near a restaurant. This represents a failure of object detection and avoidance: the system did not identify the duck as an obstacle requiring evasive action, or did not execute such action even after detection.

A human safety operator was in the vehicle but did not intervene to prevent the collision. It is not established whether the operator had time to react, what the operator's attentional state was, or what performance standards govern when a safety operator must take manual control to avoid animals.

Avride restricted its testing area and began running simulations in response. The company investigated a separate allegation that the vehicle failed to stop at a stop sign and found no evidence to support it. Whether the simulation improvements will prevent similar failures with animals, or whether the system was ever tested to detect and avoid non-human obstacles, is not established.

Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

summary:
An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride in Austin, Texas struck and killed a mother duck in the Mueller Lake neighborhood, triggering significant local concern about self-driving car safety. A resident reported on social media that the vehicle, which had a human safety operator present, did not slow down or stop after hitting the duck that had been nesting near a local restaurant. The incident gained attention because neighbors were familiar with this particular duck, and some residents have since collected the duck's eggs and placed them in an incubator.

Avride confirmed the vehicle was operating in autonomous mode at the time of the incident. The company investigated claims that the vehicle failed to stop at a stop sign and found no evidence supporting this allegation, stating the vehicle made complete stops at all relevant intersections. In response, Avride has restricted its testing area to exclude certain streets around the lake and is now conducting simulations to improve the technology and prevent similar situations while maintaining safety performance.
